dedupe_keys.name: uk dale uk domestic appliance level electricity dataset

description: UK-DALE records electricity demand from five UK homes: whole-house mains power and individual appliance power every six seconds in each house, and whole-house voltage and current at 16 kHz in houses 1, 2 and 5. The final release is April 2017 and includes 4.3 years of data for house 1. The 2015 Scientific Data paper by Kelly and Knottenbelt describes the recording system and the January 2015 release, and the author's page notes a correction on compressed storage of the 16 kHz files. Coverage: five houses in the United Kingdom. Access: the disaggregated data as a 3.5 GB zipped CSV file from the UKERC Energy Data Centre, which hosts the dataset, with other formats described on the author's page. Licence: set by the UKERC Energy Data Centre; free. Caveats: five homes only, and the dataset is no longer updated. Simulation uses are benchmarking appliance disaggregation, appliance load models and household demand profiles. Related records: the ECO data set, the IDEAL household energy dataset and the UK Energy Demand Research Project smart meter trials.
